intro.text: Expeditors is a global logistics company headquartered in Bellevue, Washington. The Company employs trained professionals in 171 district offices and numerous branch locations located on six continents linked into a seamless worldwide network through an integrated information management system. Services include the consolidation or forwarding of air and ocean freight, customs brokerage, vendor consolidation, cargo insurance, time-definite transportation, order management, warehousing and distribution and customized logistics solutions.

notes.text: Airfreight services : “Airfreight demand remained strong during the quarter, with record global air tonnage increasing approximately 13% year-over-year, driven primarily by continued growth in South Asia, where export tonnage increased most notably. Hyperscaler demand, which also includes shipments from Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers supporting AI infrastructure, was a significant driver of volume growth, while air capacity remains constrained by limited fleet expansion and ongoing new aircraft delivery delays. Capacity was also impacted by aircraft redeployments that affected Asia-Europe e-commerce, stemming from European Union regulations meant to curb the flow of de minimis imports. At the same time, China-U.S. e-commerce tonnage has nearly recovered to what it was prior to the U.S. termination of de minimis shipments in May 2025. Adding geopolitical events to this mix, airfreight rates remained elevated during the quarter, with demand outpacing available capacity.”

nodes.name: Customs brokerage and other services

notes.text: Customs brokerage and other services : “All of the products in our customs brokerage and other services continued to generate double-digit growth during the quarter, supported by strong customer demand across transportation management, distribution, and supply chain solutions. Much of the strength in our customs brokerage business was from tariff-related additional-line fees and post-entry activity that began in Q3 2025. However, growth during the most recent quarter was driven by significant new business wins, higher declaration volumes, and broad-based customs services across all regions, from both new and existing customers. Demand from AI hyperscalers and other high-value technology customers continued to drive growth across a diverse range of geographies and business sectors. Growth during the quarter was particularly strong in our Transcon road freight and warehousing and distribution businesses, with robust demand from large technology customers.”

nodes.name: Ocean freight and ocean services

notes.text: Ocean freight and ocean services : “After the flattening we saw in Q2’26, ocean volumes increased 7% year-over-year in Q3, with particularly strong comparative growth in September and across Asia export markets. Significant congestion at major Asian ports and transshipment hubs impacted the ocean markets, as capacity was idled and port operations were halted as a result of three back-to-back typhoons. Nevertheless, demand was consistently healthy and we were able to lean into our longstanding carrier relationships to secure the capacity we needed to support both existing and new customers amidst these service disruptions. The strength of our global network and world class operating teams enabled us to maintain service continuity and respond effectively as conditions deteriorated. We expect congestion and supply chain challenges to persist through the remainder of 2026.”

notes.text: Accounting for income taxes involves significant estimates and judgments. We are subject to taxation in various states and in many foreign jurisdictions including the People’s Republic of China, including Hong Kong, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Mexico, Canada, Netherlands and the United Kingdom. Management believes that our tax positions, including intercompany transfer pricing policies, are reasonable and are consistent with established transfer pricing methodologies and norms. We are under, or may be subject to, audit or examination and assessments by the relevant authorities in respect of these particular jurisdictions primarily for 2009 and thereafter. Sometimes audits and examinations result in proposed assessments where the ultimate resolution could result in significant additional tax, penalties and interest payments being required. We establish liabilities when, despite our belief that the tax return positions are appropriate and consistent with tax law, we conclude that we may not be successful in realizing the tax position. In evaluating a tax position, we determine whether it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained upon examination, including resolution of any related appeals or litigation processes, based on the technical merits of the position and in consultation with qualified tax advisors.

nodes.name: Working capital & other

notes.text: We maintain international unsecured bank lines of credit for short-term working capital purposes. A few of these credit lines are supported by standby letters of credit issued by a United States bank or guarantees issued by the Company to the foreign banks issuing the credit line. At December 31, 2024, borrowings under these credit lines were $31 million and we were contingently liable for $68 million from standby letters of credit and guarantees. The standby letters of credit and guarantees primarily relate to obligations of our foreign subsidiaries for credit extended in the ordinary course of business by direct carriers, primarily airlines, and for duty and tax deferrals available from governmental entities responsible for customs and value-added-tax (VAT) taxation. The total underlying amounts due and payable for transportation and governmental excises are properly recorded as obligations in the accounting records of the respective foreign subsidiaries, and there would be no need to record additional expense in the unlikely event the parent company is required to perform.

nodes.name: Operating cash flow

notes.text: Our principal source of liquidity is cash and cash equivalents and cash generated from operating activities. Net cash provided by operating activities for the year ended December 31, 2024 was $723 million, as compared with $1,053 million for 2023. This $330 million decrease is primarily due to changes in working capital as we made investments to finance our business growth in the second half of 2024. At December 31, 2024, working capital was $1,593 million, including cash and cash equivalents of $1,148 million. Other than our recorded lease liabilities, we had no long-term obligations or debt at December 31, 2024. Management believes that our current cash position and operating cash flows will be sufficient to meet our capital and liquidity requirements for at least the next 12 months and thereafter for the foreseeable future, including meeting any contingent liabilities related to standby letters of credit and other obligations.

analysis: Revenue was $10.6B in FY2024, up 14% year over year. Customs Brokerage and Other Services was the largest line at 36% of revenue. Ocean Freight and Ocean Services added $0.79B year over year (up 33%), 60% of the total change.

Operating profit was $1.0B, a 9.8% margin (down 0.3 points year over year). Of the extra revenue versus FY2023, 8% reached operating profit, below the 10% margin then. Total costs grew 14% against revenue growth of 14%. The fastest-growing cost line was Sales & marketing (+19%). Net earnings were $0.81B, up 8% year over year. The effective tax rate was 25.9%.

Operating cash flow was $0.72B (down 31% year over year), 89% of net earnings. Non-cash charges added back $0.06B of depreciation and amortization and $0.06B of share-based compensation. Working capital and other items used $0.21B. Capital expenditures of $0.04B left free cash flow of $0.68B.
